maria (runtime): I pulled the nsys trace for the regression reported on the staging pool. weird pattern: kernel selection flips mid-request when prefetch KV hits are high. nvtx ranges look suspicious.
aj (perf): Can you attach the perfetto/NSYS snippet? also did the perf-alert correlate with a model change or batching param tweak?
kevin (infra): perf-alert showed increased tail latency ~3.2% starting 2026-02-05 03:12 UTC. no model changes deployed at that time, but we did adjust batching heuristics in canary.
sasha (ml): batching heuristics change would explain runtime choosing a different kernel variant for shorter vs longer seqs. but flipping mid-request implies the runtime thinks sequences are changing mid-exec or KV cache interaction causes fallback.
maria (runtime): attaching the important snippet from the nsys capture (trimmed):

```
# nvtx timeline (excerpt)
[push] nvtxRangeStartA("request:1234:prepare")
  [push] nvtxRangeStartB("kv:prefetch")
  kernel: matmul_qkv_fwd_variant_v2  (40ms)
  [pop] nvtxRangeEndB()
  kernel: matmul_qkv_fwd_variant_v1  (55ms)  # different kernel, higher latency
[pop] nvtxRangeEndA()
```

maria (runtime): note the second kernel was selected after the KV prefetch range ended. suspect: our kernel selector sees different max_seq or kv_cache state and switches to the safer (slower) kernel for remainder.
aj (perf): can we make nvtx ranges carry attributes so selection logic can read them in postprocessing? e.g., include :role=kv-prefetch, req_id, cache_hit_rate
maria (runtime): we can't change kernel selector runtime logic to read NVTX — it's not part of control plane. but we can standardize range names and add per-request span ids so traces dont merge across requests. that will let offline tooling correlate kernel choices with request context.
kevin (infra): +1 on unique per-request span ids. also request: add a thin tag for "batching-mode" so we know if the request was in microbatch vs single.
sasha (ml): if we add batching-mode and kv-hit attributes at NVTX time, we can compute correlation: kernel_variant vs kv_hit_rate vs batch_size.
perf-bot: alert: regression detected in staging pool: 3.2% p95 increase. trace_id=trace-0x9a7c
aj (perf): maria, can you push a follow-up instrument change that does:

```
// pseudo C++ nvtx helpers
void nvtx_push_req_span(uint64_t req_id, const char* mode) {
  char buf[128];
  snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "req:%llu mode=%s", req_id, mode);
  nvtxRangePushA(buf);
}

void nvtx_push_kv_span(uint64_t req_id, int hits) {
  char buf[128];
  snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "req:%llu kv_prefetch hits=%d", req_id, hits);
  nvtxRangePushA(buf);
}
```

maria (runtime): looks good. i want to keep range naming short to avoid nvtx label truncation in nsight. maybe use hex req ids: `r=0xabc123` and short keys: `m=mb` or `m=single`, `k=5` for hits.
kevin (infra): remember NVIDIA NVTX has a 127 char limit for names on some tools. shorter is safer.
sasha (ml): also consider adding a sticky span at request start: `nvtxNameOsThreadA("req=r=0xabc123")` so we can quickly filter per-thread in perfetto.
aj (perf): good idea; also capture the kernel selection decision in logs (lightweight) so we have deterministic mapping: when kernel-selector chooses variant X, emit: `LOG(DEBUG): selector chose=kern_v1 reason=max_seq>512 kv_state=partial`.
maria (runtime): actioning: i'll land an instrumentation PR that:
- add per-request short NVTX spans with `r=... m=...`
- tag kv-prefetch spans with `k=N` (prefetch hits)
- add a lightweight kernel-selector log line with request id and reason
- ensure nvtx push/pop balanced in hot path (no extra allocations)

kevin (infra): +1. can you also add a perfconfig for nsys perf runs to capture kernel names + nvtx names? something like:

```
nsys profile --output trace --capture-range nvtx --trace=cuda,cudnn --sample=none \
  --force-overwrite --stop-on-exit
```

maria (runtime): I will. i'll also put a small perfetto recipe for tracing across a few warmup requests to reproduce the flip.
sasha (ml): once we have the spans, i'll run the correlation analysis and check if certain batch-size thresholds cause the selector to prefer v1 mid-request.
aj (perf): quick followups:
- we should add a unit test that simulates a KV prefetch hit pattern and asserts the kernel selector stays consistent when expected
- consider a guard in selector: disallow switching kernel variant once a kernel for the request has started unless we detect a safety concern

maria (runtime): agree on guard. will prototype: `if (kernel_started_for_req && !safety_issue) keep_variant`.
kevin (infra): timeline: aim for small PR this week, trace run on canary early next week, and revert/rollback plan if we see regressions.
maria (runtime): i'll open the PR and @aj to review the perf config. tagging sasha for correlation tests.
aj (perf): i'll review. thanks.
sasha (ml): i'll set up a perfetto dashboard after traces come in.
perf-bot: note: scheduled nsys capture for canary tomorrow 06:00 UTC. will include full NVTX labels if present.
maria (runtime): thanks everyone. quick note — keep nvtx usage lockfree on the hot path; use stack-allocated buffers only. ping me if you spot potential allocations in the change.
kevin (infra): acknowledged.
aj (perf): ack.
sasha (ml): ack, thanks.
